lead.hed: An Arlington tomb sentinel reminded Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth's delegation to keep silent and respectful at the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier
lead.insight: A U.S. Army sentinel guarding the Tomb of the Unknown Soldier moved toward Hegseth's group on the memorial steps Wednesday after laughter was heard, and from a distance called out that all visitors will maintain an atmosphere of silence and respect at all times. Hegseth, his wife and senior aides had been taking pictures and talking following a Veterans Day event at Arlington National Cemetery. Chief Pentagon spokesman Sean Parnell said the Secretary and the Department have always honored the sacrifices of American service members, and that the soldier correctly and respectfully reminded everyone to maintain decorum. The moment came two days after House Republicans sent impeachment articles against Hegseth to committee rather than voting on them directly.

political.hed: House Republicans sent impeachment articles against Defense Secretary Pete Hegseth to committee in a 211-204 vote, likely stalling any floor vote until January
political.insight: Rep. Thomas Massie, R-Ky., had charged Hegseth with negligence and illegal activity over counternarcotics strikes in the Caribbean and Pacific, the February strike on Iran without congressional approval, retaliation against Sen. Mark Kelly, and the capture of Venezuelan President Nicolas Maduro without a declaration of war. Sending the articles to the Judiciary Committee instead of a direct vote likely delays any reckoning until January, when Democrats take over the House majority with 256 seats to the Republicans' 168. A two-thirds vote would still be needed to force Hegseth from office. Hegseth called the effort a political farce at a rare Pentagon news conference ahead of the vote.

political.hed: Midterm exit polls show the Republican coalition eroding among young, high-income and college-educated voters
political.insight: Republicans fell to about 43 percent of voters earning over $100,000 and just 25 percent of voters under thirty, erasing 2024 gains with both groups. Support among non-college-educated voters, the core of the party's 2024 House majority, also slipped to roughly 2018 levels. The analysis argues the president's hold on the party has weakened and the fight over what comes after him, between market-oriented conservatives and national populists, is now unavoidable.

tech.hed: Britain is investing $120 million in a North Atlantic drone and AI network called Atlantic Net to track Russian submarines
tech.insight: The U.K. Ministry of Defense announced Tuesday that the Royal Navy will build a network of drones, sensors and AI systems, dubbed Atlantic Net, meant to better protect undersea cables and detect Russian submarine activity in the North Atlantic. The investment is the latest sign allied navies are leaning on unmanned and AI-driven sensing rather than only crewed ships to watch contested undersea terrain.

tech.hed: A free year of ChatGPT Plus has now reached more than 20,000 transitioning veterans and servicemembers
tech.insight: Veterans are using the free access to organize job searches, rehearse interviews and explore civilian career paths, with community partners hosting more than a dozen trainings for nearly 1,000 members of the military community. Workshops in Reston, Virginia, and at the American Legion's national convention in Louisville drew veterans and military spouses who built custom tools to support their transitions. The program was marked on Veterans Day.

culture.hed: Rings of Power's third season finally reaches the forging of the Ruling Ring, and one critic sees hope for a fresh start
culture.insight: The review notes the season finally reaches the forging of the Ruling Ring after two seasons where Tolkien's Elves came across more like impatient men with pointy ears and Gandalf arrived in Middle-earth missing his memory and his clothes. With Sauron now in open war against Elves and Men, the critic sees the latest episodes offering some hope that the show's adaptation can find its footing and honor the source material it has strayed from.

culture.hed: Brian Kilmeade and Heritage President Kevin Roberts dug into the stories that forged America's founding
culture.insight: The conversation, tied to Kilmeade's new book on America's founding era, argues that as the nation marks 250 years of independence, recovering the people and defining moments behind the founding matters as much as celebrating it. Heritage frames the discussion as a chance to rediscover the principles that made the American experiment possible, rather than treat the anniversary as pageantry alone.

culture.hed: Why treating every political fight as 'with us or against us' borrows a claim only God can rightly make
culture.insight: The essay, written by a professor who counsels politically anxious students, argues that treating every political question as a forced binary is theologically presumptuous: Jesus could rightly divide mankind into for-Him and against-Him because He is the God-man judging ultimate reality, but political movements that borrow that same absolute framing set themselves in a place no human cause can occupy. The piece pushes back on the pressure young conservatives feel to treat moderation as cowardice, arguing mature political judgment requires resisting binary thinking rather than embracing it.
